### 3.2. Construction of B

In this subsection, we will use the equivalence of pairs $\operatorname{AB}$ to construct the morphism of pairs

$$ \operatorname{B}:(\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G})\longrightarrow(\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}},\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}) $$

in $\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ .

#### 3.2.1.

There is a monoidal action

$$ (\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G})\otimes(\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G),\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G}))\to(\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G),\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})) $$

which can be written as a monoidal functor

$$ (\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G})\to(\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(G),\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G}))\otimes(\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(G),\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G}))\simeq(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))^{\otimes 2}. $$

#### 3.2.2.

The image of the factorization (and monoidal) unit in $\operatorname{Sph}_{G}$ under

$$ \operatorname{Sph}_{G}\to\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})^{\otimes 2} $$

is the factorization algebra $R_{\check{G}}$ , the regular representation of $\check{G}$ considered as a representation of the group $\check{G}\times\check{G}$ . Geometrically, this is the pushforward of

$$ \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{reg}}} $$

under

$$ \operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{reg}}\to\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{reg}}\times\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{reg}}. $$

#### 3.2.3.

Thus, we obtain a monoidal morphism of pairs

$$ (\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G})\to R_{\check{G}}\operatorname{-FactMod}[(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))^{\otimes 2}]. $$

By Theorem 1.5.6 (taking $\mathcal{Y}_{0}=\operatorname{pt}/\check{G}^{2}\times X_{dR}$ , $\mathcal{Y}=\operatorname{pt}/\check{G}\times X_{dR}$ , and $\mathcal{S}_{0}=(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}})^{2}$ ), there is a morphism

$$ (\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}},\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}})\to R_{\check{G}}\operatorname{-FactMod}[(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))^{\otimes 2}] $$

that is an equivalence on the eventually coconnective part of each component.

#### 3.2.4.

As when we were constructing $\operatorname{AB}$ , we would like to say that $\operatorname{Aff}_{G}$ is compactly generated and that its compact generators are sent to eventually coconnective objects. However, it is unlikely that $\operatorname{Aff}_{G}$ is compactly generated. Again, we are saved by fusability, since

$$ \operatorname{Aff}_{G,{\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}\operatorname{-QLisse}}}\subset\operatorname{Aff}_{G} $$

is compactly generated by compact generators that are sent to

$$ R_{\check{G}}\operatorname{-FactMod}(\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})^{\otimes 2})^{>-\infty}. $$

Using fusability of $\operatorname{FactRes}_{\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})\to\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}(\operatorname{Aff}_{G})$ , we are able to lift the resulting functor

$$ \operatorname{Aff}_{G,{\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}\operatorname{-QLisse}}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}} $$

to all of $\operatorname{Aff}_{G}$ , and we obtain our desired morphism

$$ \operatorname{B}:(\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G})\longrightarrow(\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}},\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}) $$

in $\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ .

### 3.3. B is a Pointwise Equivalence

#### 3.3.1.

After applying the appropriate factorization restrictions, $\operatorname{Aff}_{G}$ and $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ are fusable as factorization $\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})$ -module categories. Thus, in order to show that $\operatorname{B}$ is an equivalence, it suffices to show that

$$ \operatorname{B}_{x_{0}}:\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}} $$

is an equivalence of categories.

#### 3.3.2.

In [DT25], Dhillon and Taylor construct a version of (pointwise) Bezrukavnikov’s equivalence in the monodromic, Betti setting. In other words, there are two key differences from our setting. First, the stack on the geometric side is

$$ \tilde{\operatorname{Fl}}_{G}/I_{0}=I_{0}\backslash LG/I_{0} $$

instead of

$$ \operatorname{Fl}_{G}/I=I\backslash LG/I. $$

Second, the sheaf theory on the geometric side is ind-constructible sheaves with nilpotent singular support

$$ \operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Nilp}} $$

instead of

$$ \operatorname{D-mod} $$

and correspondingly, the spaces that appear on the spectral side are the Betti versions.

#### 3.3.3.

Let us summarize the construction in [DT25] (or, rather, the analogue of their construction in our unipotent monodromy, de Rham setting). The monoidal category

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})} $$

has an obvious action on the category

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G}) $$

which can be identified via $\operatorname{AB}_{x_{0}}$ with

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}). $$

Furthermore, the action of $\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}$ on $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})$ has a tautological datum of compatibility with the action of

$$ \operatorname{bi-Whit}(LG)=\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(LG)) $$

on $\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})$ . However, the latter action can be identified with the action of

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}) $$

on $\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G})$ via pullback. Thus, we obtain a monoidal functor

$$ \iota^{!}:\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G})}(\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}))\simeq\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}). $$

#### 3.3.4.

Then, because of Morita-theoretic properties of $\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G})$ as a $\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}$ - $\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G})$ bimodule, $\iota^{!}$ has a fully faithful left adjoint $\iota_{!}$ . Furthermore, the kernel of $\iota^{!}$ consists precisely of the infinitely connective objects of $\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}$ , so we obtain an equivalence

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}/\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren}),\leq-\infty}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}). $$

#### 3.3.5.

Finally, we renormalize as follows. On the spectral side, the full subcategory of pseudocompact objects is

$$ \operatorname{Psc}(\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}))=\operatorname{Coh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}). $$

On the other hand, on the geometric side we have an equivalence

$$ \operatorname{Psc}(\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})})\simeq\operatorname{Psc}(\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}/\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren}),\leq-\infty}) $$

and the pseudocompact objects in $\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}$ are precisely the compact objects (i.e. objects of $\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{I}$ that are compact after forgetting down to $\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})$ on either side). Thus, we obtain an equivalence

$$ \operatorname{B}^{\operatorname{classical}}:\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}\overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}). $$

#### 3.3.6.

Our task now is to identify $\operatorname{B}_{x_{0}}$ , the fiber at $x_{0}$ of our factorization functor $\operatorname{B}$ , with $\operatorname{B}^{\operatorname{classical}}$ . To do so, it suffices to show that

$$ \operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}\overset{\operatorname{B}_{x_{0}}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}\overset{\Psi_{x_{0}}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{QCoh}_{\operatorname{co}}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}\underset{(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}})_{x_{0}} $$

identifies with

$$ \iota^{!}:\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}\overset{\operatorname{B}^{\operatorname{classical}}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G})\overset{\Psi}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}). $$

#### 3.3.7.

By construction, we already have an identification of

$$ \displaystyle\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}\overset{\operatorname{B}_{x_{0}}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}} \displaystyle\overset{\Psi_{x_{0}}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{QCoh}_{\operatorname{co}}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}\underset{(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}})_{x_{0}} \displaystyle\longrightarrow\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}\times\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}})_{x_{0}} $$

with

$$ \displaystyle\operatorname{D-mod}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})^{(I,\operatorname{ren})}\overset{\operatorname{B}^{\operatorname{classical}}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}) \displaystyle\overset{\Psi}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}) \displaystyle\longrightarrow\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\times\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}) $$

(i.e. the functors to $\operatorname{End}(\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}))$ defined by the two actions are the same because we used $\operatorname{AB}_{x_{0}}$ to construct the latter action).

#### 3.3.8.

Therefore, all that remains to be shown is that the datum of compatibility - between the action of $\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}$ on $\operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G})$ and the action of $\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G})$ - given by $\Psi_{x_{0}}\circ\operatorname{B}_{x_{0}}$ is isomorphic to the tautological one. But this follows from the fact that the pair

$$ (\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})) $$

carries a monoidal action of the pair

$$ (\operatorname{QCoh}(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})) $$

which has a tautological datum of compatibility with the monoidal action of $(\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G}$ ); and when restricted to $x_{0}$ , the former action identifies with the action of

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times})) $$

on

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}) $$

given by pullback along

$$ \tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\longrightarrow\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}(D_{x_{0}}^{\times}) $$

which factors through $\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}$ . This concludes the proof of Theorem 0.2.8.

## 4. Iwahori FLE

### 4.1. Construction of IFLE

In this subsection, we will construct the Iwahori Fundamental Local Equivalence

$$ \operatorname{IFLE}:(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})\longrightarrow(\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})). $$

as a morphism in $\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$ .

#### 4.1.1.

We recall that there is an action

$$ \operatorname{act}:\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})\otimes\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}\to\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}} $$

obtained from the action of $\operatorname{Sph}_{G}$ on $\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}$ via the monoidal functor

$$ \operatorname{Sat}_{G}^{\operatorname{nv}}:\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})\to\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}\simeq\operatorname{Sph}_{G}. $$

We have

$$ \operatorname{act}(R_{\check{G},\operatorname{Op}}\boxtimes Vac)\simeq Vac $$

so

$$ R_{\check{G},\operatorname{Op}}\boxtimes Vac\to\operatorname{coact}(Vac). $$

#### 4.1.2.

We can extend the action $\operatorname{act}$ to

$$ (\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\otimes(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})\to(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}) $$

by composing the action of $(\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G})$ on $(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})$ with the monoidal morphism of pairs

$$ \operatorname{B}^{\operatorname{nv}}:(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\to(\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}},\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}})\simeq(\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G}). $$

Now analogously with Section 5.3 of [ABC+24a], we consider the right adjoint of the above action

$$ (\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})\to(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\otimes(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}). $$

This factors through

$$ (\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})\to\operatorname{coact}(Vac)\operatorname{-FactMod}[(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\otimes(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})] $$

and factorization restriction along $R_{\check{G},\operatorname{Op}}\boxtimes Vac\to\operatorname{coact}(Vac)$ gives a map to

$$ (R_{\check{G},\operatorname{Op}}\boxtimes Vac)\operatorname{-FactMod}[(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\otimes(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})] $$

which is the same as

$$ R_{\check{G},\operatorname{Op}}\operatorname{-FactMod}(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\otimes Vac\operatorname{-FactMod}(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}) $$

or in other words

$$ R_{\check{G},\operatorname{Op}}\operatorname{-FactMod}(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\otimes(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}). $$

However, by Theorem 1.5.6, there is a morphism of pairs

$$ (\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\to R_{\check{G},\operatorname{Op}}\operatorname{-FactMod}(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}),\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})) $$

that is an equivalence on the eventually coconnective part in each component.

#### 4.1.3.

Then we are able to obtain a map from

$$ (\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}) $$

to

$$ (\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\otimes(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}) $$

since on the first component, as noted in loc. cit.

$$ \operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}\to\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G})\otimes\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}} $$

is t-exact so

$$ \operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}^{c}\subset\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}^{b} $$

is sent to the eventually coconnective part of

$$ R_{\check{G},\operatorname{Op}}\operatorname{-FactMod}(\operatorname{Rep}(\check{G}))\otimes\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}. $$

On the second component,

$$ \operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}\otimes\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}\to\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}} $$

is bounded on the right for each fixed bounded object of $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}$ . Then so is

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})\otimes\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}\to\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}} $$

and thus the right adjoint

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}\to\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})\otimes\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}} $$

is bounded on the left for each fixed bounded object of $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}$ . Therefore,

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}^{c}\subset\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}^{b} $$

is sent to the eventually coconnective part of

$$ R_{\check{G},\operatorname{Op}}\operatorname{-FactMod}(\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}))\otimes\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}. $$

#### 4.1.4.

This morphism defines a coaction of

$$ (\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})) $$

on $(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})$ , or in other words, an action of

$$ (\operatorname{IndCoh}^{!}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{!}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})). $$

#### 4.1.5.

Parallel to Section 6.1 of [ABC+24a], we can consider the morphism of pairs

$$ \displaystyle(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}) \displaystyle\to(\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{\hat{\mathfrak{g}}-mod}_{\operatorname{crit}}),\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{\hat{\mathfrak{g}}-mod}_{\operatorname{crit}})) \displaystyle\overset{\operatorname{\overline{DS}^{enh,rfnd}}}{\to}(\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})) $$

as a morphism of $(\operatorname{IndCoh}^{!}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{!}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}))$ -modules (in the monoidal sense).

We thus obtain a morphism of pairs from

$$ (\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}) $$

to

$$ \operatorname{Fun}_{\operatorname{IndCoh}^{!}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})}((\operatorname{IndCoh}^{!}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{!}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})) $$

which identifies with

$$ (\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})). $$

This morphism of pairs is what we will denote by $\operatorname{IFLE}$ .

#### Remark 4.1.6.

$\operatorname{IFLE}$ intertwines (more precisely, has intertwining data) the action of

$$ (\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G}) $$

on

$$ (\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}},\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}) $$

and the action of

$$ (\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}},\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}) $$

on

$$ (\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}}),\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})) $$

via the monoidal equivalence of algebra objects in $\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$

$$ \operatorname{B}:(\operatorname{Sph}_{G},\operatorname{Aff}_{G})\simeq(\operatorname{Sph}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}},\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}). $$

The reason is that everything from Appendix E.10.4 to the end of E.11 in [ABC+24a] carries over mutatis mutandis to the setting of pairs (and Lemma E.10.3 is replaced by our construction of $\operatorname{B}$ ).

### 4.2. Reduction to the Pointwise Equivalence

We will now show that to prove $\operatorname{IFLE}$ is an equivalence of pairs, it is sufficient to prove that it is an equivalence at $x_{0}$ . Our strategy is similar to that for $\operatorname{FLE}$ in Section 6.2 of [ABC+24a].

#### 4.2.1.

For the rest of the subsection, let us assume the following

#### Proposition 4.2.2.

$$ \operatorname{IFLE}_{x_{0}}:\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}} $$

is an equivalence.

This proposition will be proven in the latter subsections of this section.

#### 4.2.3.

We note that on each stratum $X_{x_{0}}^{(n),\circ}$ of $\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}$ ,

$$ \operatorname{IFLE}_{X_{x_{0}}^{(n),\circ}}:(\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})_{X_{x_{0}}^{(n),\circ}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{X_{x_{0}}^{(n),\circ}} $$

identifies with

$$ \displaystyle\operatorname{FLE}_{X^{(n),\circ}}\boxtimes\operatorname{IFLE}_{x_{0}}: \displaystyle(\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}})_{X^{(n),\circ}}\boxtimes\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to \displaystyle\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mon-free}})_{X^{(n),\circ}}\boxtimes\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}} $$

which is an equivalence because $\operatorname{FLE}$ is an equivalence.

#### 4.2.4.

Now it suffices to show that $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}$ is compactly generated and that $\operatorname{IFLE}$ preserves compacts. This will demonstrate that $\operatorname{IFLE}$ has a continuous right adjoint as a morphism of sheaves of categories, which implies that whether it is an equivalence can be checked strata by strata.

#### 4.2.5.

In the same way that $\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}$ is generated by the images of the compact generators of $\operatorname{Rep}(L^{+}G)$ under

$$ \operatorname{ind}_{L^{+}G}^{(\hat{g}_{\operatorname{crit}},L^{+}G)}:\operatorname{Rep}(L^{+}G)\to\operatorname{KL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}, $$

the category $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}$ is generated by the images of the compact generators of the factorization $\operatorname{Rep}(L^{+}G)$ -module category $\operatorname{Rep}(I)$ under

$$ \operatorname{ind}_{I}^{(\hat{g}_{\operatorname{crit}},I)}:\operatorname{Rep}(I)\to\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}} $$

which can be verified by mimicking the construction from Appendix B.14 of [ABC+24a].

#### Remark 4.2.6.

The argument below was explained to us by Lin Chen.

#### Lemma 4.2.7.

An object $c\in\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})$ is compact if for every $\lambda\in\Lambda_{G}$ , the *-pushforward along

$$ \operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}} $$

of

$$ c(\lambda)=c\otimes(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}\to\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})^{!}\mathcal{O}(\lambda) $$

is compact in $\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})$ .

#### Proof.

The map

$$ \operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}} $$

is a base change of

$$ \tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\longrightarrow\check{\mathcal{N}}/\check{G}\longrightarrow\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}. $$

The second map is a closed embedding, so it detects coherent objects. Thus, it suffices to show the claim for

$$ \tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}/\check{G}\longrightarrow\check{\mathcal{N}}/\check{G} $$

and by fppf descent, we can reduce to showing the claim for the springer resolution

$$ \tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}\longrightarrow\check{\mathcal{N}} $$

which factors as

$$ \tilde{\check{\mathcal{N}}}\longrightarrow\check{\mathcal{N}}\times\check{G}/\check{B}\longrightarrow\check{\mathcal{N}}. $$

Since the first map is a closed embedding, it detects coherent objects, and it suffices to show the claim for

$$ \check{G}/\check{B}\longrightarrow\operatorname{pt}. $$

But on $\check{G}/\check{B}$ , the claim that the $\lambda$ -twisted global sections functors jointly detect coherent objects follows from the fact that $\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{G}/\check{B})=\operatorname{IndCoh}(\check{G}/\check{B})$ is generated by a finite number of $\mathcal{O}(\lambda)$ , and thus

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\check{G}/\check{B})\simeq R\operatorname{-mod} $$

for a smooth proper dg algebra $R$ , where the forgetful functor $R\operatorname{-mod}\to\operatorname{Vect}$ corresponds to a finite sum of twisted global sections functors. But this clearly detects coherent objects. ∎

#### Proposition 4.2.8.

The functor $\operatorname{IFLE}$ preserves compact objects.

#### Proof.

$\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}$ is compactly generated by the verma modules $\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}$ , so we want to show that $\operatorname{IFLE}(\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})$ is compact. By the above lemma, it suffices to show that

$$ (\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}\to\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{*}(\operatorname{IFLE}(\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})(\lambda)) $$

is compact. However, $\operatorname{IFLE}$ is compatible with $\operatorname{B}$ , so twisting by $\lambda$ on the spectral side corresponds to convolving with the Wakimoto $J_{\lambda}$ on the geometric side, i.e.

$$ \operatorname{IFLE}(\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})(\lambda)=\operatorname{IFLE}(\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}\star J_{\lambda}). $$

Furthermore,

$$ (\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}\to\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{*}\circ\operatorname{IFLE}:\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

corresponds to the functor

$$ \mathcal{C}^{I}\longrightarrow\mathcal{C}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\mathcal{C}) $$

for $\mathcal{C}=\operatorname{\hat{\mathfrak{g}}-mod}_{\operatorname{crit}}$ , which preserves compacts. $\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}$ is compact, and since convolving with a Wakimoto is an equivalence, so is $\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}\star J_{\lambda}$ , and we are done. ∎

### 4.3. Iwahori-Hecke Temperedness

In this subsection, we will introduce the notion of Iwahori-Hecke Temperedness and explain how to use it to prove Proposition 4.2.2.

#### 4.3.1.

Consider the fiber of $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ at $x_{0}$ :

$$ \operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}\underset{(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x_{0}}})_{x_{0}}\simeq\operatorname{IndCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}). $$

Denote by $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec,temp}}$ the category

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}\underset{\check{\mathfrak{g}}/\check{G}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}). $$

There is a fully faithful embedding

$$ \operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec,temp}}\to\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}} $$

which has a monoidal continuous right adjoint

$$ \operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}\to\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec,temp}}. $$

#### 4.3.2.

Let $\boldsymbol{M}$ be a $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ -module category. Then we can consider

$$ \boldsymbol{M}^{\operatorname{temp}}=\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec,temp}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\boldsymbol{M} $$

and the adjunction

$$ \operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec,temp}}\rightleftharpoons\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}} $$

induces an adjunction

$$ \boldsymbol{M}^{\operatorname{temp}}\rightleftharpoons\boldsymbol{M}. $$

#### Definition 4.3.3.

We say that a $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ -module category $\boldsymbol{M}$ is Iwahori-Hecke tempered if the above adjunction is an equivalence.

#### Remark 4.3.4.

We use the adverb Iwahori-Hecke in order to distinguish our notion from the analogous notion of temperedness defined in Section 7.1 of [ABC+24a]. We will refer to the latter as spherical temperedness.

#### 4.3.5.

Now let

$$ \operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}} $$

be the image of

$$ \check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}\to\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}} $$

and note that

$$ \operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec,temp}}\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\operatorname{QCoh}((\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge})}(\operatorname{QCoh}((\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}),\operatorname{QCoh}((\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})). $$

For a $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ -module category $\boldsymbol{M}$ , since $\operatorname{QCoh}((\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})$ is rigid, entirely parallel to Corollary 7.1.8 in [ABC+24a], we can conclude that

$$ \boldsymbol{M}^{\operatorname{temp}}\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\operatorname{QCoh}((\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge})}(\operatorname{QCoh}((\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}),\operatorname{QCoh}((\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\boldsymbol{M}) $$

and thus on the full subcategory of Iwahori-Hecke tempered $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ -module categories, the assignment

$$ \boldsymbol{M}\mapsto\operatorname{QCoh}((\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\boldsymbol{M} $$

is conservative.

#### 4.3.6.

Here is our strategy for proving Proposition 4.2.2. It is similar to the argument given throughout Section 7.2 to 7.4 of [ABC+24a]. First, we will construct a commutative diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\boldsymbol{=}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}).}} $$

Then, we will show that the vertical arrows are fully faithful embeddings with the same essential image, which will demonstrate that the top arrow

$$ \displaystyle\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}} \displaystyle\longrightarrow\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}} \displaystyle\overset{\operatorname{Id}\otimes\operatorname{IFLE}_{x_{0}}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}} $$

is an equivalence. Since the first morphism of the composition is an equivalence, this will imply that the second morphism of the composition is also an equivalence.

Finally, we will show that $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}$ and

$$ \operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\simeq\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}) $$

are both Iwahori-Hecke tempered, which will allow us to conclude that $\operatorname{IFLE}_{x_{0}}$ is an equivalence.

### 4.4. IFLE is a Pointwise Equivalence

In this subsection, we will check the various claims in order to prove Proposition 4.2.2.

#### Proposition 4.4.1.

There is a commutative diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\boldsymbol{=}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}).}} $$

#### Proof.

We claim that there is a commutative diagram in $\operatorname{FactModCat_{x_{0}}}$

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Whit}^{!}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})\otimes\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})\otimes\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}).}} $$

where the right vertical arrow is given by $*$ -pushforward along

$$ \operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\times\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}. $$

For the left vertical arrow, consider the following paradigm: for $\mathcal{M}$ a category with an action of $\operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(LG)$ , there is a map

$$ \operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G}}{\otimes}\mathcal{M}^{I}\to\mathcal{M} $$

taking Whittaker coinvariants yields

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G}}{\otimes}\mathcal{M}^{I}\to\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\mathcal{M}) $$

and by duality we obtain

The left vertical arrow is this functor with $\mathcal{M}=\operatorname{\hat{\mathfrak{g}}-mod}_{\operatorname{crit}}$ .

The above commutative diagram can be constructed by following the construction in Appendix E.10 of [ABC+24a] and upgrading it to pairs mutatis mutandis.

Then we can invoke the compatibility of $\operatorname{AB}$ and $\operatorname{IFLE}$ with $\operatorname{B}$ to curry and obtain

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit}}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}})}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\boldsymbol{=}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\operatorname{IndCoh}^{*}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G}}^{\operatorname{mer}}).}} $$

The desired diagram is the specialization of the above to $x_{0}$ . ∎

#### Proposition 4.4.2.

The right vertical arrow

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})\longrightarrow\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

is fully faithful with essential image

$$ \operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}}\subset\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}), $$

the full subcategory of $\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})$ of objects that are set-theoretically supported on

$$ \operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}=\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}\subset\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}. $$

#### Proof.

$\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}$ and $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ are both rigid like their spherical counterparts, so we can apply the argument in the proof of Proposition 3.6.5 in [ABC+24a] largely unchanged: the functor

$$ \displaystyle\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}) \displaystyle\simeq\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}) \displaystyle\to\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}) $$

has a continuous and monadic right adjoint. The same is true of the pushforward

$$ \operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}} $$

because

$$ \check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B}\to\operatorname{LS_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}} $$

is the springer resolution, and thus proper and surjective. The functor

$$ \operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})\longrightarrow\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

induces a morphism between the two monads, and to see that it is an isomorphism of monads, it suffices to show that it is an isomorphism on the level of endofunctors. However, both monads are given by the action of the algebra object

$$ (\operatorname{pr_{1}}:(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\to(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})^{!}\mathcal{O}_{(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}} $$

of $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ on $\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})$ . ∎

#### Proposition 4.4.3.

The left vertical arrow

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

is fully faithful with essential image

$$ \operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}}\subset\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}). $$

#### Proof.

Like the affine grassmannian, the affine flag variety $\operatorname{Fl}_{\check{G},x_{0}}$ is also ind-proper. Thus, the proof of full faithfulness is similar to the argument given in Section 7.3 of [ABC+24a]: just as in the spherical case, for a category $\boldsymbol{C}$ with an action of the loop group $LG$ at the critical level,

$$ \boldsymbol{C}^{\operatorname{Aff-gen}}=\operatorname{D-mod}_{\frac{1}{2}}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G,x_{0}})\underset{\operatorname{Aff_{G,x_{0}}}}{\otimes}\boldsymbol{C}^{I}\longrightarrow\boldsymbol{C} $$

is fully faithful and has a continuous right adjoint. But this implies that

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\boldsymbol{C}^{\operatorname{Aff-gen}})=\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff_{G,x_{0}}}}{\otimes}\boldsymbol{C}^{I}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\boldsymbol{C}) $$

is fully faithful. Taking $\boldsymbol{C}=\operatorname{\hat{\mathfrak{g}}-mod}_{\operatorname{crit}}$ gives us fully faithfulness of

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{\hat{\mathfrak{g}}-mod}_{\operatorname{crit}})\simeq\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

as desired.

Furthermore, the functor

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\overset{c\ \mapsto\ \boldsymbol{1}_{\operatorname{Aff}_{G}}\otimes c}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}} $$

generates the target; therefore, to show that the essential image of

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

is contained in

$$ \operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}}, $$

it suffices to show that the essential image of the composition

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

is contained in $\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}}$ . However, the above composition is isomorphic to the composition

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\overset{\operatorname{IFLE}_{x_{0}}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}) $$

whose essential image is clearly contained in $\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}}$ .

Now, it remains to show that

$$ \operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}} $$

is essentially surjective.

Since the functor is fully faithful, it suffices to show that it generates the target; for which, in turn, it suffices to show that the composition

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{Whit}^{*}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})_{x_{0}}\underset{\operatorname{Aff}_{G,x_{0}}}{\otimes}\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}} $$

generates the target.

Because we have

$$ (\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}})_{\operatorname{red}}=\bigsqcup_{\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}\in\check{\lambda}^{+}}\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}, $$

the objects

$$ \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}\in\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}} $$

compactly generate $\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}}$ .

We claim that the Verma modules

$$ \mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}=\operatorname{ind}_{I}^{(\hat{g}_{\operatorname{crit}},I)}k_{\check{\lambda}}\in\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}} $$

are sent to $\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}$ under the functor $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\to\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}}$ .

To see this, we will adapt the argument in [FG10] that shows $\operatorname{FLE}$ sends the Weyl modules $\mathbb{V}^{\check{\lambda}}$ to $\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{reg}}}$ :

On one hand, we have the isomorphism

$$ \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}\simeq\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}) $$

and unwinding definitions yields

$$ \operatorname{End}(\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})=\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{ind}_{I}^{(\hat{g}_{\operatorname{crit}},I)}k_{\check{\lambda}},\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{I}(k_{\check{\lambda}},\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})=:(\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}})_{\check{\check{\lambda}}}^{I^{0}}. $$

For any $M\in\operatorname{\hat{\mathfrak{g}}-mod}_{\operatorname{crit}}$ , there is a map

$$ (M)_{\check{\lambda}}^{I^{0}}\to M^{\hat{\mathfrak{n}}_{+}}\to H^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathfrak{n}((t)),\mathfrak{n}[[t]],M\otimes\Psi_{0}), $$

which is the content of Lemma 3 of [FG10]. Taking $M=\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}$ gives us a map

$$ \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}\to H^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathfrak{n}((t)),\mathfrak{n}[[t]],\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}\otimes\Psi_{0}), $$

where the latter identifies with the desired image of $\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}$ . Thus, it suffices to show that this map is an isomorphism.

Analogously to the $\check{\lambda}$ -regular case, we have that the above map has the structure of a morphism of modules over the lie algebroid $N^{*}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}/\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}$ , and that $\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}$ is irreducible as a $N^{*}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}/\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}$ -module. Therefore, this map must be injective and it suffices to compute and compare the characters of both sides as in Section 5 of [FG10].

First, let us compute the character of $\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}}$ . Let

$$ J=\{\alpha_{i}\in\Delta|\langle\alpha_{i},\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}\rangle=0\} $$

and denote by $\check{P}_{J}$ the parabolic subgroup of $\check{G}$ corresponding to $J$ . Now note that $\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}$ is the set of operators of the form

$$ \{\partial_{t}+\Sigma_{\Delta}\ t^{\langle\alpha_{i},\check{\lambda}\rangle}f_{i}+v(t)+\frac{w}{t}\ |\ v(t)\in\check{\mathfrak{b}}[[t]],w\in O\} $$

modulo the action of $\check{N}[[t]]$ , where

$$ O=\{w\in\check{\mathfrak{b}}\ |\ w+\Sigma_{J}f_{i}\operatorname{mod}\check{\mathfrak{n}}_{J}\in\mathcal{N}_{\check{\mathfrak{m}}_{J}}\}. $$

However, this is the same as

$$ \{\partial_{t}+\frac{1}{t}(\Sigma_{\Delta}f_{i}-(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}))+v(t)+\frac{w}{t}\ |\ v(t)\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{\mathfrak{b}}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1},w\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)O(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}\} $$

modulo the free action of $(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{N}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}$ .

Consider $O\cap\check{\mathfrak{m}}_{J}$ , which carries a free and transitive action of the group $\check{N}\cap\check{M}_{J}$ . There is a surjective homomorphism of groups

$$ \phi:(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{N}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}\to\check{N}\cap\check{M}_{J} $$

which picks out the constant term, and there is a surjective morphism

$$ \displaystyle\{\partial_{t}+\frac{1}{t}(\Sigma_{\Delta}f_{i}-(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}))+v(t)+\frac{w}{t}\ |\ v(t)\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{\mathfrak{b}}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1},w\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)O(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}\} \displaystyle\overset{\pi}{\longrightarrow}O\cap\check{\mathfrak{m}}_{J} $$

which picks out the constant term of $w$ . $\pi$ is equivariant with respect to $\phi$ , so we have

$$ \operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}\simeq\pi^{-1}(0)/\operatorname{ker}(\phi) $$

and thus

$$ \operatorname{char}(\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}})=\operatorname{char}(\operatorname{Fun}(\pi^{-1}(0)))/\operatorname{char}(\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{ker}(\phi))). $$

$\pi^{-1}(0)$ is

$$ \{\partial_{t}+\frac{1}{t}(\Sigma_{\Delta}f_{i}-(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}))+v(t)+\frac{w}{t}\ |\ v(t)\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{\mathfrak{b}}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1},w\in(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{\mathfrak{n}}_{J}(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}\} $$

so

$$ \operatorname{char}(\operatorname{Fun}(\pi^{-1}(0)))=\Pi_{n>0}(1-q)^{-l}\cdot(\Pi_{\alpha\in\Phi_{J}^{+}}\Pi_{n\geq 0}(1-q^{n+1})^{-1})\cdot(\Pi_{\alpha\in\Phi^{+}\setminus\Phi_{J}^{+}}\Pi_{n\geq 0}(1-q^{n+\langle\alpha,\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}\rangle})^{-1}). $$

On the other hand,

$$ \operatorname{ker}(\phi)=(\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)\check{N}[[t]](\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho})(t)^{-1}\cap\operatorname{exp}(t\check{\mathfrak{n}}[[t]]) $$

so

$$ \operatorname{char}(\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{ker}(\phi)))=(\Pi_{\alpha\in\Phi_{J}^{+}}\Pi_{n\geq 0}(1-q^{n+1})^{-1})\cdot(\Pi_{\alpha\in\Phi^{+}\setminus\Phi_{J}^{+}}\Pi_{n\geq 0}(1-q^{n+\langle\alpha,\check{\lambda}+\check{\rho}\rangle})^{-1}). $$

Therefore,

$$ \operatorname{char}(\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\check{\lambda}-\operatorname{nilp}}})=\Pi_{n>0}(1-q)^{-l}. $$

Finally, to compute the character of $H^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathfrak{n}((t)),\mathfrak{n}[[t]],\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}\otimes\Psi_{0})$ , we follow what is done in Section 5.2 of [FG10] essentially verbatim except with the finite Weyl module $V^{\lambda}$ replaced with the finite Verma module $M^{\lambda}$ . Then, we find that

$$ \operatorname{char}(H^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathfrak{n}((t)),\mathfrak{n}[[t]],\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}\otimes\Psi_{0}))=\Pi_{n>0}(1-q)^{-l} $$

as desired. ∎

#### Proposition 4.4.4.

$\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})$ is Iwahori-Hecke tempered.

#### Proof.

For tautological reasons, there is an isomorphism

$$ \operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}\simeq(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge}\underset{(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}. $$

Because $(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge}$ is passable like its spherical counterpart $(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{mon-free}}^{\wedge}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\operatorname{IndCoh}((\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge}\underset{(\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}) \displaystyle\simeq\operatorname{IndCoh}((\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge})\underset{\operatorname{QCoh}((\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}})_{\operatorname{nilp-mon}}^{\wedge})}{\otimes}\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}} $$

as $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ -module categories. However, the action of $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ on the right hand side comes from the action of $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ on $\operatorname{QCoh}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}$ , which factors through $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec,temp}}$ . ∎

Finally, we will show that $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}$ is Iwahori-Hecke tempered.

#### Remark 4.4.5.

Here the argument diverges significantly from the proof of the analogous result, Proposition 7.2.6 of [ABC+24a] given in Section 7.4. This is because the action of $\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}$ on $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}$ is not t-exact. We will instead use the following weaker property.

#### Lemma 4.4.6.

If

$$ \mathcal{F}\in\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec},\leq-\infty} $$

and

$$ c\in\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{c}\subset\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{b}, $$

then

$$ \mathcal{F}\star c\in\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{\leq-\infty}. $$

#### Proof.

Since $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}$ is generated by verma modules, we may take $c=\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}$ .

The functor

$$ \Gamma:\operatorname{D-mod}_{\operatorname{crit}}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})\longrightarrow\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}} $$

was studied in [FG09]. For an object $\mathcal{F}\in\operatorname{Aff}_{G}$ ,

$$ \Gamma(\mathcal{F})=\mathcal{F}\star\mathbb{M}^{0}. $$

Using similar methods, one can study a twisted version

$$ \Gamma^{\check{\lambda}}:\operatorname{D-mod}_{\operatorname{crit},\check{\lambda}}(\operatorname{Fl}_{G})\longrightarrow\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}} $$

which sends

$$ \Gamma^{\check{\lambda}}(\mathcal{F})=\mathcal{F}\star\mathbb{M}^{\check{\lambda}}. $$

Now the claim follows from the bounded cohomological amplitude of each $\Gamma^{\check{\lambda}}$ . ∎

#### Proposition 4.4.7.

$\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}$ is Iwahori-Hecke tempered.

#### Proof.

We want to show that

$$ \operatorname{temp}:\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{temp}} $$

is an equivalence. Since it is a colocalization, it suffices to show that it is conservative. Note that the functor $\operatorname{IFLE}^{\operatorname{temp}}$

$$ \operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{temp}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}})^{\operatorname{temp}}\simeq\operatorname{IndCoh}(\operatorname{Op}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}\underset{\operatorname{LS}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{mer}}}{\times}(\check{\mathfrak{n}}/\check{B})_{x_{0}}) $$

is an equivalence. Thus, since $\operatorname{IFLE}$ preserves compacts, so does $\operatorname{temp}$ . It follows that it suffices to show that $\operatorname{temp}$ is conservative on compact objects. However, all compacts are bounded in $\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}$ , and using the fact that

$$ \operatorname{cone}(\operatorname{temp}(\boldsymbol{1}_{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}})\to\boldsymbol{1}_{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}})\in\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec},\leq-\infty} $$

we can conclude that the cone of the counit map

$$ \operatorname{cone}((\operatorname{temp}(c)\to c)\simeq\operatorname{cone}(\operatorname{temp}(\boldsymbol{1}_{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}})\to\boldsymbol{1}_{\operatorname{Aff}_{\check{G},x_{0}}^{\operatorname{spec}}})\star c\in\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{\leq-\infty}. $$

Therefore, if $\operatorname{temp}(c)=0$ , then $c\in\operatorname{IKL}(G)_{\operatorname{crit},x_{0}}^{\leq-\infty}$ which implies $c=0$ since c is also bounded. This shows that $\operatorname{temp}$ is conservative on compact objects, as desired. ∎
